summary: The note explains how Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) have coped with supply chain disruptions since the pandemic began in early 2020, drawing on quotes from industry practitioners. It covers strategies such as supplier diversification, technology-enabled transparency, strong vendor relationships, vendor-managed inventory, green supply chains, and cross-training employees. The overall message is that adaptability and innovation make SMEs stronger and better prepared.
one_line: SMEs can handle post-pandemic supply chain disruption through diversification, technology, vendor partnerships, VMI, sustainability, and cross-trained staff.
key_facts: The coronavirus pandemic, beginning in early 2020, exposed the fragility of global supply chains and pressured SME vendor relations.
Disruptions from lockdowns and labor shortages had a domino effect that lasted into late 2023.
Lean, just-in-time inventory models left many businesses unable to respond to sudden changes in supply and demand.
Lisa Moreno, CEO of a mid-sized tech devices firm, said: "You either learned to be agile, or you were out of the race."

Thomas Keller, a Supply Chain Consultant based in Chicago, recommends diversifying supply sources; a small automotive parts manufacturer avoided severe disruption by using local subcontractors and suppliers from different regions when its main Asian supplier's lead times went haywire.

A consortium of industry analysts reported on October 13, 2023 that technology integration (AI, IoT, blockchain) in supply chain management is mandatory, giving SMEs real-time data, predictive analytics and transparent transaction logs.

Terry Smith, Operations Manager at a family-owned consumer goods company, used a cloud-based supply chain management platform to trace material shortages to a supplier's supplier on another continent.

Julia Espinoza, a Supply Chain Director at a mid-sized manufacturer in Texas, said on November 6, 2023 that regularly engaging suppliers on plans, risks and contingencies makes them more likely to go the extra mile.
Strong vendor relationships can bring more favorable payment terms, joint ventures in product development, and shared logistics solutions.

Greg Patel, founder of an electronics company, switched to vendor-managed inventory (VMI) in September 2023, which improved inventory accuracy and strengthened supplier bonds while freeing focus for marketing and R&D.

On December 1, 2023, a small organic skincare brand overhauled its packaging supply chain to use locally produced, biodegradable materials, reducing its carbon footprint and international shipping risk.
Miranda Johnson, HR Manager at a small e-commerce retailer, said cross-training staff lets the team handle customer service, inventory and supplier negotiations during peak periods.
